sentenceSets.sentence: The physician distinguished between somatic symptoms—muscle aches and fatigue—and psychological factors that might contribute to the patient's illness.

answerChoices.reasoning: Physical means relating to the body; while somatic symptoms are physical, 'physical' is broader and can include external physical factors, whereas 'somatic' specifically refers to the body's tissues and organs.

Corporeal means having a body or being material; while somatic is corporeal, 'corporeal' is more philosophical and refers to the body's material nature, whereas 'somatic' is specifically medical/biological.
Bodily means relating to the body; while somatic symptoms are bodily, 'bodily' is more general, whereas 'somatic' specifically refers to body tissues as distinguished from germline cells.

Systemic means affecting the entire body or system; while somatic symptoms affect the body, 'systemic' specifically means spread throughout a system, whereas 'somatic' can refer to localized body tissue.

Organic means relating to living organisms or organs; while somatic refers to the body, 'organic' emphasizes living material and functional systems, whereas 'somatic' refers to body tissues as distinguished from germline.
Visceral means relating to internal organs; while somatic symptoms can involve organs, 'visceral' specifically refers to internal organs, whereas 'somatic' refers more broadly to body tissues.
Tangible means perceptible or real; while somatic symptoms are tangible, 'tangible' is more general and refers to anything that can be perceived or touched.
Symptomatic means showing signs of disease; while the somatic symptoms indicate disease, 'symptomatic' refers to the manifestation of illness, not the body location.
Mental means relating to the mind; the sentence contrasts somatic symptoms with psychological factors, making mental the opposite domain.
Psychological means relating to the mind or emotions; the sentence explicitly contrasts somatic symptoms with psychological factors.
Emotional means relating to feelings; the sentence contrasts somatic (body) symptoms with psychological factors, of which emotion is a part.

sentenceSets.sentence: Rather than resorting to medication, the therapist recommended somatic practices like breathing exercises and progressive muscle relaxation to address the patient's anxiety.

answerChoices.reasoning: Physical means relating to the body; while somatic practices involve the body, 'physical' can include external physical exercise, whereas 'somatic' specifically means working through bodily sensation and awareness.

Kinesthetic means relating to body movement and sensation; while somatic practices involve kinesthetic awareness, 'kinesthetic' emphasizes movement, whereas 'somatic' emphasizes awareness of bodily sensations.
Bodily means relating to the body; while somatic practices are bodily, 'bodily' is more general, whereas 'somatic' specifically refers to awareness and regulation of bodily processes.
Holistic means treating the whole person; while somatic practices can be holistic, 'holistic' emphasizes treating the whole being, whereas 'somatic' specifically focuses on bodily experience.
Behavioral means relating to behavior or conduct; while somatic practices involve behavioral changes, 'behavioral' refers to external actions, whereas 'somatic' emphasizes internal bodily experience.
Alternative means different from the usual; while somatic practices are alternatives to medication, 'alternative' describes the approach, not the specific body-based nature.
Therapeutic means having healing benefits; while somatic practices are therapeutic, 'therapeutic' describes the effect, not the body-focused method.
Meditative means involving focused attention or mindfulness; while somatic practices can be meditative, 'meditative' emphasizes mental focus, whereas 'somatic' emphasizes bodily sensation.
Pharmaceutical means relating to drugs or medication; the therapist specifically recommended somatic practices 'rather than resorting to medication,' the opposite.
Cognitive means relating to thinking and reasoning; somatic practices address bodily sensation and awareness, not cognitive thought processes.
Mental means relating to the mind; somatic practices work through the body, not through mental processes or thinking.

sentenceSets.sentence: In genetics, somatic mutations affect an organism's body cells but cannot be passed to offspring, whereas germline mutations can alter heredity.

answerChoices.reasoning: Genetic means relating to genes or heredity; while somatic mutations are genetic, 'genetic' is broader and includes both somatic and germline mutations.
Acquired means obtained or developed after birth; while somatic mutations can be acquired, 'acquired' is less specific and doesn't distinguish somatic from germline mutations.
Cellular means relating to cells; while somatic mutations affect body cells, 'cellular' is broader and can apply to any mutations in cells, including germline.

Epigenetic means relating to non-DNA factors affecting gene expression; while somatic changes can be epigenetic, 'epigenetic' is distinct from somatic mutations and doesn't imply specific body tissue changes.
Nonhereditary means not inherited; while somatic mutations are nonhereditary, this term doesn't specify that they affect body cells, whereas 'somatic' specifically refers to body tissue.
Environmental means caused by environmental factors; while somatic mutations can be caused by environmental factors, 'environmental' describes the cause, not the cellular location.
Spontaneous means occurring without external cause; while some somatic mutations are spontaneous, 'spontaneous' describes the origin, not the body-cell distinction.
Chromosomal means relating to chromosomes; while somatic mutations can be chromosomal, 'chromosomal' describes the type of mutation, not the body-cell location.
Hereditary means inherited or passed to offspring; the sentence emphasizes that somatic mutations 'cannot be passed to offspring,' the opposite of hereditary.
Germline means relating to reproductive cells; the sentence explicitly contrasts somatic mutations with germline mutations as opposite categories.
Inherited means passed from parent to offspring; somatic mutations are not inherited, they affect only body cells, the opposite.
